# Allowlist for the public-repo leak guard — ci actions/leak-guard v2 (v1.27.0).
# Entry kinds (v2 rules): `key:<regex>` is the ONLY way to suppress an
# identifier finding (guid, entra-tenant) — and only when the finding is the
# VALUE of that key (`key`/`"key"` + [:=] + optional quote); an entry with `/`
# is a LITERAL single-file path (no metacharacters, no trailing slash); any
# other regex is matched against a NON-identifier finding's TEXT only. No
# directory scopes, no regex paths, no text entry can hide a GUID.
# Baseline: full-tree dry run 2026-10-29 with entra-tenant + azure-subscription
# + aws-account armed — 0 entra-tenant, 0 azure-subscription findings. The
# finding-by-finding triage is in the PRs that added/adapted this file.

# ── Hostnames (text) ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# The product edge hostnames: live/edge, live/identity, live/onprem,
# live/storage-*, live/observability-alerting and the incident/record docs
# configure or name them; the edge configuration in this public repo is the
# source of truth for them (published deliberately).
^(www|mail|send|preview)\.qnsc\.vn$
^(rova|opshub)(-dev)?\.qnsc\.vn$
^rova\.dev\.qnsc\.vn$
^rova-assets(-dev)?\.qnsc\.vn$
^opshub-api-dev\.qnsc\.vn$
^kb-dev\.qnsc\.vn$
^kb-api-dev\.qnsc\.vn$
# Dead pre-rename name, kept in the EKS teardown record:
^rally-api-dev\.qnsc\.vn$
# Dead EKS hostname, teardown record only:
^rova-api-eks-dev\.qnsc\.vn$
# Example PR-preview hostname in the platform design record:
^rova-412\.preview\.qnsc\.vn$

# ── Mail addresses (text) ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Operator alert alias in live/* and docs (public by design):
^devops@qnsc\.vn$
# SECURITY.md's public security-contact address:
^security@qnsc\.vn$
# Product send-only mailboxes, both documented spellings (noreply-<product>
# and <product>-noreply):
^noreply(-[a-z0-9-]+)?@qnsc\.vn$
^([a-z0-9]+-)?noreply@qnsc\.vn$

# ── Literal single-file paths (non-identifier findings only) ─────────────────
# The VPC subnet CIDRs of the two runtime stacks (policy: file scope, never a
# directory). A private address anywhere else in the tree fails.
live/runtime-dev/main.tf
live/runtime-prod/main.tf
# That file's operator fixture address:
scripts/owner/test_bootstrap_state.sh

# ── key: entries (identifier findings; the finding must be the key's value) ──
# Microsoft well-known first-party constants used by the Entra audit and
# live/identity (Graph app, Exchange Online app, Microsoft services tenant):
key:client_id
key:GRAPH_APP_ID
key:EXCHANGE_APP_ID
key:MICROSOFT_TENANT
key:appId"?
key:id"?
# Graph object/role ids in the Entra audit fixtures and report keys (the
# leading (?<![\w-]) in the matcher keeps `Id` from riding on `clientId`):
key:resourceAppId"?
key:resourceId"?
key:appRoleId"?
# live/identity/proxmox.tf: the all-zero default-access app role id (a Microsoft
# well-known constant, not an identifier of ours):
key:app_role_id
key:appOwnerOrganizationId"?
key:request-id"?
# Fabricated AWS KMS key ids in the orphan-audit fixtures:
key:KeyId"?
key:TargetKeyId"?
# Named constants/variables holding fabricated ids (test suites, audit helper):
key:DEFAULT_ROLE_ID
key:STUB_SUBSCRIPTION
key:graph_id
key:graph_app
key:ROLE_FIXTURE_ID
key:SP_FIXTURE_ID
key:TENANT_FIXTURE_ID
key:FIXED_CREDENTIAL_ID
